answer.rationale: The release cannot be rolled back (compliance hard-constraint), ruling out rollback_release. Regional failover is a big-bang move under peak settlement load and the relevant memory (memory_b2) addressed latency during a March degradation where traffic shifted cleanly—not the same failure signature here. Circuit breakers on the write path would shed customer writes, violating the primary objective. Add-capacity is plausible but slow to provision and the climb has been 90 minutes; it does not address root cause and may not land in time. Route-read-replicas directly targets the write-path latency mechanism: memory_b5 documents that dashboard/report queries were contending with transactional writes on the primary, and offloading reads recovered write latency the same day. With settlement traffic at daily peak and 5x p99 on writes, the most likely single intervention that (a) needs no rollback of the security patch, (b) preserves all customer writes, and (c) can be applied within one action window is diverting read/report traffic to replicas to relieve primary I/O. Verification: memory_b5 confirms the pattern and same-day recovery. Guardrail: monitor settlement write error rate for 5 minutes post-cutover; if write latency does not begin recovering within 15 minutes, escalate to add_capacity in the next window.
